run_ref.note: the archived run, unchanged. It supplies the estimator configuration, not the number.

claim: Your hypothesis splits. The NUMBER is wrong by about an order of magnitude: at your envelope -- f_s = 520 Hz, t_exp = 0.45 ms, T_obs = 5 s per rung, epsilon = 10 nm -- the per-realisation relative error on the PSD-recovered f_c of a SINGLE bead is 29.1 +/- 0.9 % sd, not 'at or below 3 %'. The MECHANISM is right: what binds is the observation length and not the samples-per-relaxation-time convention. Turning the camera on and off moves the scatter by 28.5 -> 29.1 %, about 2 % relative; going 5 s -> 32.3 s moves it 29.1 -> 9.2 %, a factor 3.2. So 520 fps is not what is costing you, and r2's finding[0] 2*pi disagreement is indeed a naming difference -- but 520 fps is not sufficient either, because sufficiency was never about f_s.

answering_quantity.why: Exactly what r3 asked for: the per-realisation relative error on the recovered corner frequency for one bead, with exposure integration and Gaussian localisation noise applied to the trajectory before fitting. Measured on exact Ornstein-Uhlenbeck trajectories rather than on a BD run, because an exact OU sampler is unbiased at any step size -- the detector effect being measured is a few percent and Euler-Maruyama error would sit on top of it.

achieved_precision.basis: Standard error on a standard deviation, sd/sqrt(2(n-1)), over n = 512 independent single-bead realisations (4 batches x 128). r3 asked for one percentage point of resolution because the decision is binary at ~3 %; 0.91 clears that, and the answer is 29.1, so the decision is not close.

requirements.from: Same number as r2, and the second time its basis has been restated -- this one is measured rather than inferred. Single-bead scatter with the camera in the model: 29.1 +/- 0.9 % at your 5 s (T_obs/tau_k = 309.7), 9.2 +/- 0.3 % at 32.3 s (T_obs/tau_k = 2000.9). Neither is under your 3 %. Reaching 3 % by observation length alone needs roughly (9.2/3)^2 x 32.3 s ~ 300 s per rung, which your D-3 cost argument already rules out at six rungs and three sizes -- so the honest reading is that a single-bead per-rung f_c at 3 % is not reachable by acquisition length, and the per-rung precision has to come from somewhere else: more beads per rung, or taking gamma from the drag slope rather than from f_c.

basis_refs.note: the camera layer: boxcar over t_exp, then additive Gaussian epsilon.

requirements.from: LOWERED from r2's 620 Hz, and it is now your own gate's number rather than this repository's convention. r2 asked for 620 Hz because this repository samples at tau_k/10; measured, that convention does not bind here. At 520 Hz (8.39 samples per tau_k) the camera costs 2 % relative on the scatter, against the 220 % that observation length costs. Your G14c f_s >= 10 f_c = 99 Hz is the binding form. This is deliberately not a hard requirement and deliberately not derived from your number -- it is this side agreeing that the looser convention is the correct one at this envelope.

UNCHANGED from r2 and unaffected by everything above. Derived analytically from variance inflation (epsilon/l_k)^2 at l_k = 33.98 nm recomputed here. Still hard: it is a bias on the equipartition alpha and does not average down over rungs or over beads, which is what distinguishes it from the scatter this document is about.

regime.name: T_obs/tau_k
regime.tolerance: the binding group -- 29.1 % single-bead scatter at 310, 9.2 % at 2001
regime.why_this_tolerance: Measured, not inherited. Scatter scales roughly as 1/sqrt(T_obs): a factor 6.5 in T_obs buys 3.2 in scatter, and sqrt(6.5) = 2.5, so slightly better than the naive scaling. This is the only group in this thread that has ever been shown to move the answering quantity by more than a few percent.

regime.name: samples_per_tau_k
regime.why_this_tolerance: r2 stated a 10 floor by convention and r3 asked whether it binds. It does not: 8.394 against 10 costs 2 % relative on the scatter. What the group DOES control is the estimator bias of r4 (+0.8 % at 10, +7.9 % at 2), which is a property of the fit and not of the acquisition.

regime.name: u = t_exp/tau_k
regime.tolerance: u << 1; deflation of var(x) is u/3
regime.why_this_tolerance: Zero on this side without the camera layer, 0.027876 with your exposure. Per r4's correction the deflation is 0.93 %, not 1.86 %.

regime.name: epsilon/l_k
regime.meaning: localisation noise against the thermal amplitude
regime.why_this_tolerance: Shared exactly, because the camera layer was run at your assumed epsilon. At 0.29429 it inflates var(x) by 8.66 %, which is the whole of the 5 % budget before the ladder fit starts.

assumptions.name: camera_model
assumptions.mine: Boxcar average over t_exp = 0.45 ms, then additive Gaussian epsilon = 10 nm, applied to positions sampled at 24 steps per exposure and framed at 517.8 Hz (103 integration steps; 520.0 Hz is not an integer number of steps, and the 0.4 % shortfall is stated rather than rounded away).
assumptions.theirs: 0.45 ms exposure, epsilon ~10 nm assumed pending P8

worth.note: Relative effect of the whole camera on sigma_f_c_single at 5 s: 28.5 % without it, 29.1 % with. It moves the BIAS much more than the scatter -- +2.53 % to +4.52 % -- which is the r4 story, not this one.

assumptions.note: r2 recorded this as a gap and r3 asked for it. It is now built, checked against closed-form answers, and shared rather than differing.

assumptions.name: particle_count
assumptions.mine: One bead per realisation, 512 independent realisations. This is the n_replicas = 1 configuration r2 gaps[3] asked for, obtained as 512 separate single-bead fits rather than as an ensemble-averaged PSD.
assumptions.note: The 1000-replica objection of r2 finding[3] does not apply to this document. Every number here is a single-bead number.

assumptions.name: wall_drag
assumptions.mine: No wall. gamma_corr is your Faxen factor applied to bulk Stokes, not a wall this side simulated.
assumptions.note: Unchanged since r2 and still the largest structural difference. h0 remains unanswered.

assumptions.name: dimensionality
assumptions.mine: Per-component, one coordinate. The OU process is the exact x-dynamics of a separable harmonic trap.

worth.note: f_c is per-component and carries no dim.

assumptions.name: inertia
assumptions.mine: Overdamped; tau_p/tau_k = 7.30e-5 recomputed from your primitives

assumptions.name: drift
assumptions.theirs: z drift under ~0.3 um per rung

assumptions.name: estimator
assumptions.mine: Unweighted least squares of S0/(1+(f/f_c)^2) over the whole one-sided Welch PSD -- the archived run's own fit, kept deliberately so this document and r4 measure the same estimator.

worth.note: Bias, not scatter: +4.52 % with the camera at 5 s, +2.53 % without. Separate from the 29.1 % reported here, and it does not shrink with T_obs.

assumptions.note: Carried forward unresolved from r4. The 29.1 % is a scatter and is not affected by the bias, but any comparison of CENTRAL VALUES between the two sides still needs this settled.

gaps.what: A single-bead per-rung f_c at 3 % is not reachable by observation length.
gaps.why: 9.2 % at 32.3 s, and scatter goes as 1/sqrt(T_obs), so 3 % needs ~300 s per rung.
gaps.consequence: r3's premise -- that 3 % is available and the question is only whether the envelope delivers it -- does not hold. The decision moves from 'is 520 fps enough' to 'where does per-rung precision come from'.
gaps.would_need: More beads per rung, or gamma from the drag slope rather than from f_c. Both are yours to weigh; neither is simulable here without the wall.

gaps.what: What f_c's recoverability is, once the estimator is fixed.
gaps.why: Carried from r4. The bias is still in place; only the scatter is reported here.
gaps.consequence: Central values are still not comparable between the two sides at the ~1 % level.
gaps.would_need: A weighted fit, re-verified against exact OU. No new trajectory.

gaps.why: Unchanged since r2: no runner, one height.
gaps.consequence: r1's headline question is still open after five rounds.

findings.what: r3's hypothesis splits cleanly: the mechanism is right, the number is ~10x out.
findings.am_says: sigma_f_c_single <= 3 %, and what binds is T_obs rather than the samples-per-tau convention.
findings.bd_says: 29.1 +/- 0.9 % measured at the stated envelope. The second clause is confirmed: camera on/off is 2 % relative, T_obs 5 s -> 32.3 s is a factor 3.2.

findings.what: The camera is not the problem, which is the opposite of what both sides expected.
findings.am_says: Exposure and localisation noise act directly on the equipartition alpha, so they were treated as the thing to model.
findings.bd_says: On the SCATTER of f_c they are worth 2 % relative. They are worth much more on the BIAS (+2.5 % -> +4.5 %), and on var(x) and therefore on alpha. Two different quantities were being conflated -- the camera matters for alpha, it does not matter for how reproducible f_c is.

findings.what: r2's f_s >= 620 Hz is withdrawn in favour of AM's own 99 Hz.
findings.am_says: G14c wants f_s >= 10 f_c = 99 Hz; 520 fps clears it 5.3x.
findings.bd_says: Agreed, and measured. The tau_k/10 convention that produced 620 Hz is a convention; at this envelope the 16 % shortfall against it costs 2 % relative on the answering quantity. Where the convention does earn its keep is the estimator bias, which is a fit property.

out_of_scope: h0 and the wall, carried over unchanged.
The equipartition alpha itself. This document is about f_c's reproducibility; the camera's effect on alpha is r4's corrected 7.7 %.
Whether 300 s per rung is affordable. That is D-3's arithmetic, not this side's.
